name: Talbot Rice Gallery
funding: University of Edinburgh gallery; 2025-26 shows credit ECA, Creative Scotland, Henry Moore Fdn, British Council, MGS, Polish culture ministry.

name: BALTIC Centre for Contemporary Art
funding: Opened July 2002 with £33.4M of Arts Council lottery capital; Gateshead Council backed the building. Corporate supporters include Tommee Tippee and NorthStandard.

name: GoMA
funding: Run by Glasgow Life for Glasgow City Council. Glasgow Life's supporters include Creative Scotland, the Scottish Government, Art Fund, the National Lottery Heritage Fund and Bloomberg Philanthropies.

name: The Common Guild
funding: £379k income (FY2025). Creative Scotland plus grants from Ampersand, Henry Moore, Elephant Trust, Pro Helvetia, British Council Scotland, Goethe-Institut, Culture Ireland, Hope Scott Trust and individuals.

name: Compton Verney
funding: £5.07M income (FY to Mar 2026). Compton Verney Fund endowment, Arts Council NPO, members. Local firms Silson, SE-Solicitors, Goldcrest.

name: Henry Moore Institute
funding: Part of the Henry Moore Foundation, funded from its investment portfolio. Leeds City Council gives £145,743 a year to the Institute; Arts Council England funds the Yorkshire Sculpture International partnership.

name: Charleston
funding: Charity running Charleston farmhouse and its Wolfson Gallery. Gifts and grants from the Art Fund, National Lottery Heritage Fund and Arts Council England; Bloomberg Connects supplies its digital guide.

name: Bluecoat
funding: £2.4M income (FY2025); Arts Council, Liverpool City Council, Culture Liverpool.

name: FACT
funding: Arts Council England and Liverpool City Council are statutory funders. Paul Hamlyn, Jerwood, John Ellerman, Granada, Bloomberg Philanthropies and other trusts also give.

name: Mostyn
funding: £0.7M income (FY2026). Arts Council of Wales £385k, Conwy County Borough Council, Llandudno Town Council, National Gallery; Garfield Weston, Henry Moore, Ampersand, Foyle, Ashley Foundation, Mostyn Estates.
